chunks: And from his words (peace be upon him), when he passed by Talhah ibn Abd Allah and Abd al-Rahman ibn Itab ibn Asid, while they were corpses killed on the day of Jamal,

key_terms.طَلْحَة: Talhah, a prominent companion of the Prophet
key_terms.يَوْمَ الْجَمْلِ: The day of Jamal (the Battle of the Camel)

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say when passing by the corpses of Talhah and Abd al-Rahman after the Battle of the Camel?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) reflects on the Battle of the Camel, viewing the deaths of Talha and Zubayr (often associated with Abd al-Rahman in this context) not as a defeat but as a necessary purification of the community from fitnah. This narration underscores the Shia perspective that while these companions were mistaken in their stance, their intent was not apostasy, yet their rebellion against the legitimate Caliphate incurred specific spiritual consequences. The event serves as a pivotal moment in early Islamic history, illustrating the transition from the unified Rashidun era to the distinct political and theological divisions that followed.
